example.name: simple_api_endpoint
example.scenario: User asks to create a user profile API endpoint that returns user information
example.user_request: Create an API endpoint to get user profiles

step.approach: Identified: GET endpoint for user profiles Need to clarify: authentication requirements, which fields to return, whether this is for self or others viewing
step.output: Scoped request for user profile retrieval

step.approach: Created user story: As a client, I want to retrieve user profiles so that I can display user information Defined acceptance criteria with testable conditions Identified edge cases: non-existent user, private profiles, deleted users Documented security: authentication required, data exposure minimized

Designed data flow: client -> API -> auth check -> DB query -> transform -> response Defined database schema for User collection Created API contract: GET /api/users/:id with response schema Documented error codes: 401, 403, 404, 500
Created sequential tasks: 1. Add database query function 2. Create API route handler 3. Add authentication middleware 4. Implement response transformation 5. Add unit tests 6. Add integration tests

Presented all three artifacts inline Highlighted key decisions: field selection, error handling approach Asked explicitly: "Do you approve these artifacts? Reply yes to proceed or specify changes needed."

example.completion: If user approves: Switch to Code mode and execute tasks in sequence If user rejects: Update rejected artifacts and re-present

key_takeaways.takeaway: Always halt after artifacts, never proceed without approval
Make acceptance criteria testable, not vague

example.name: feature_with_frontend_and_backend
example.scenario: User asks for a bookmarking feature that allows users to save their reading position
example.user_request: Add bookmarking so users can save and restore their reading position in comics

step.approach: Questions asked: Should bookmarks be per-device or synced? What's the maximum bookmarks per user? Should there be bookmark sharing? Are bookmarks manual or auto-saved?
step.output: User clarified: auto-save, cloud-synced, per-user limit of 100

step.approach: Created user stories: - As a reader, I want my position auto-saved so I can continue later - As a reader, I want to see my bookmarks across devices Defined acceptance criteria for auto-save frequency, sync behavior Edge cases: offline changes, conflict resolution, limit enforcement Security: users can only access their own bookmarks

Backend: - Database: Bookmark collection with userId, comicId, position, timestamps - API: POST /api/bookmarks, GET /api/bookmarks, DELETE /api/bookmarks/:id - Sync logic: last-write-wins with timestamp
Frontend: - useBookmarks hook - BookmarkPanel component - SyncManager for offline handling
Data flow: reader position -> auto-save debounced -> API call -> sync service -> other devices

Phase 1: Database schema (T-1.1 Create Bookmark model) Phase 2: Backend API (T-2.1 Create bookmarks API, T-2.2 Add sync logic) Phase 3: Frontend (T-3.1 useBookmarks hook, T-3.2 BookmarkPanel) Phase 4: Integration (T-4.1 Connect to reader, T-4.2 Sync testing)

step.output: All three artifacts ready for review

key_takeaways.takeaway: Breaking into phases helps manage complexity
Sync and offline handling add significant complexity - document edge cases

example.name: rejected_artifacts
example.scenario: User reviews artifacts and requests changes before approval

step.output: requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md shown to user

step.feedback: "The sync approach with last-write-wins will cause data loss. I want a merge strategy instead."

step.approach: Changed sync logic from last-write-wins to operational transformation Updated conflict resolution strategy Revised database schema to include version vectors Updated API contracts for merge endpoints
Added tasks for merge logic implementation Added tasks for version vector management Increased complexity estimates

example.completion: User approved revised artifacts → proceed with implementation

key_takeaways.takeaway: User rejection is part of the process, not a failure
